players.name: DeMario Douglas
players.waiver_note:
A.J. Brown missed Week 8 with knee/ankle issues and probably won't be back for Week 9. With Romeo Doubs on IR with a shoulder injury, DeMario Douglas might be New England's de facto No. 1 receiver when the Patriots host the Packers this Sunday.

Douglas was targeted on three of Drake Maye's 20 pass attempts Sunday and had 3-70-1, scoring on a 48-yard catch-and-run.

The 25-year-old Douglas has scored four touchdowns over his last four games and has produced at least 65 yards in three of those contests.

Douglas has a suboptimal matchup this week against the Packers, who have been stingy to slot receivers. But Douglas gets a very favorable Week 10 matchup against the Lions, who entered Week 8 having given up more fantasy points to slot receivers than any other defense.

players.name: Caleb Douglas
players.waiver_note:
If you're going to roster a Dolphins receiver, make it Caleb Douglas.

A third-round rookie from Texas Tech, Douglas has 13-226-2 on 19 targets in four games. He's averaging 10.3 half-point PPR fantasy points per game, which ties him with Justin Jefferson for WR29 in that category. Douglas is averaging 11.9 yards per target.

Well on his way to establishing himself as the Dolphins' No. 1 receiver, Douglas is playable this week against a Lions defense that has given up the second-most passing yards.

players.name: Adonai Mitchell
players.waiver_note:
It can be nettlesome to fantasy managers when one team has an overabundance of talent at the WR position, with teammates vulturing each other's fantasy value every week. It isn't often the Jets posing this problem, but, well, here we are.

Rookie Omar Cooper Jr. had 100-yard receiving games and scored touchdowns in Weeks 6-7, looking like a star in the making. Veteran Garrett Wilson had some big games early in the season. And after a relatively quiet, zero-catch return from a finger injury in Week 7, Adonai Mitchell erupted for 7-142-1 in Week 8.

A third-year player who was a throw-in in the trade that sent CB Sauce Gardner from the Jets to the Colts, Mitchell has an appealing combination of size (6-2, 205) and speed (4.34). He's had issues with drops and focus, but Mitchell's potential is evident, and we saw on Sunday what he's capable of.

A player with this much ability should absolutely be rostered in average-sized leagues. But is Mitchell a plug-and-play waiver pickup? Probably not.

With Wilson and Cooper posing stiff target competition, and with Jets QB Geno Smith not really the sort of passer who can make multiple receivers consistently fantasy-relevant, be judicious if you intend to bid on Mitchell this week after his big game.

players.name: Antonio Williams
players.waiver_note:
With Commanders WR Terry McLaurin out for the season with a torn patellar tendon in his knee, Antonio Williams was expected to play an expanded role in McLaurin's absence, and indeed the rookie did just that in Washington's Week 8 win over Philadelphia.

Williams had 5-54-0 on seven targets against the Eagles. He led the Commanders' receivers in snaps (50) and routes (29).

The third-round rookie from Clemson should continue to be busy in the weeks to come. He's well worth rostering — especially PPR leagues.

players.name: Jakobi Meyers
players.waiver_note:
Jakobi Meyers is a capable No. 2 receiver in a good Jacksonville offense. He has 22-309-2 over seven games and is averaging an impressive 10.0 yards per route run.

Meyers has been doing his best work against man coverage and against single-high safety looks this season. Unfortunately, his next three opponents — the Ravens, Titans and Giants — tend to favor zone coverage and/or two-high safety looks. But none of those three pass defenses are to be feared, and Meyers' value could get a boost if the Jaguars decided to trade mercurial WR Brian Thomas Jr.

players.name: Ryan Flournoy
players.waiver_note:
Ryan Flournoy, the Cowboys' No. 3 receiver, has become a consistent contributor. He's had either a touchdown or 70-plus yards in four consecutive games.

A sixth-round draft pick out of Southeast Missouri State in 2024, Flournoy (pronounced "fluh-NOY") began to get involved in the Dallas passing game in 2025 and finished last season with 40-475-4. This season, he has 30-342-2 and has drawn at least four targets in all eight of his games.

Flournoy is getting plenty of action even with Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens around. Pickens has been dealing with hamstring and shoulder injuries. If either Pickens or Lamb were to miss time, Flournoy's value would soar.

Entering Week 8, Flournoy had taken 53.4% of his snaps from the slot, according to Fantasy Points Data. This week, he'll face a Colts pass defense that has given up the fifth-most fantasy points to slot receivers.

players.name: Devin Singletary
players.waiver_note:
With Tyrone Tracy Jr. on IR with a hamstring injury, the Giants come out of their bye with Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary as their top two running backs. Skattebo is ostensibly the lead back, but the Giants cut his playing time a few weeks ago when Skattebo's ball security became an issue.

The 29-year-old Singletary has been a useful jack-of-all-trades RB throughout his career. He's averaged 4.4 yards per carry over seven-plus NFL seasons and has always been a very capable pass catcher.

It's possible the Giants trade for a running back ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline. They've been mentioned among the potential suitors for the Colts' Jonathan Taylor. But if the Giants stand pat this week, Singletary might get enough touches this week against the stumbling Eagles to make him at least flex-worthy in Week 9.

players.name: Greg Dulcich
players.waiver_note:
Greg Dulcich is starting to become a reliable arrow in the Dolphins' offensive quiver. He's had at least four catches and 37 yards in four of Miami's last five games. Dulcich has had at least four receptions in three straight contests.

Dulcich gets a Week 9 matchup against the Lions, who have given up the most fantasy points to TEs this season. Opposing tight ends have blasted Detroit for 61 catches, 684 yards and 11 touchdowns - all league highs.

Dulcich is a viable streaming TE this week.

players.name: Mike Gesicki
players.waiver_note:
Touchdown streaks are fragile, and chasing touchdowns is rarely a good idea. That said, Mike Gesicki has scored a touchdown in five straight games, and Bengals QB Joe Burrow has been a touchdown machine.

Gesicki's contributions in the reception and yardage categories are intermittent. He's topped 40 receiving yards twice in seven games, and he's had three games with fewer than 10 receiving yards. Gesicki is averaging 3.4 targets and 2.4 receptions per game.

With six touchdowns on the season, Gesicki has scored a touchdown on 35.3% of his catches and 25.0% of his targets. Those are unsustainable rates.

Still, Gesicki plays in perhaps the most lethal passing attack in the league. You can't count on his run of touchdown luck to continue, but he's better positioned for good TD fortune than a lot of other tight ends in the streaming class.

players.name: Kenny Gainwell
players.waiver_note: Don't chase Kenny Gainwell simply because he had 25-140-0 rushing in Week 8. Gainwell's big day was the product of a freakishly run-heavy game script for the Buccaneers, who threw only three passes in a rain-soaked 16-0 win over the Falcons. Gainwell hadn't run for more than 18 yards in a game all season, but he's had 228 rushing yards over the last two weeks, as the Buccaneers had a similarly run-heavy game script in a Week 7 demolition of the Panthers. Gainwell is a high-end handcuff for Bucky Irving and is a worthwhile stash because of how well the Buccaneers run the ball.

players.name: Dylan Sampson
players.waiver_note: Some people might see that Dylan Sampson played 12 more snaps than Quinshon Judkins in Week 8 and think that makes Sampson a worthy waiver acquisition. Context is important. The Browns were playing from behind in most of their 27-6 loss to the Steelers on Sunday, and Sampson is Cleveland's passing-down back. Sampson had just one rushing attempt in that game. He had 6-62-0 on eight targets, but most of that came in garbage time. On the Browns' final drive of the game, Sampson caught passes on three straight plays for 33 yards. Judkins is the undisputed early-down back. Sampson's role just isn't particularly fantasy-relevant in an average (at best) Cleveland offense.

players.name: Mike Washington Jr.
players.waiver_note:
It seems inconceivable that a running back drafted sixth overall in 2025 would be relegated to a passing-down role less than halfway through his second NFL season, but that appears to be the fate of the Raiders' Ashton Jeanty.

Averaging 3.1 yards per carry going into Week 8, Jeanty was replaced by rookie fourth-round pick Mike Washington Jr. on early downs. Washington was averaging 4.9 yards per carry going into Week 8. He carried 25 times for 83 yards Sunday in the Raiders' 38-33 win over the Jets.

Washington is an extraordinary physical specimen. At this year's NFL Scouting Combine, Washington ran a 4.33 in the 40-yard dash at 223 pounds, giving him a 100th percentile speed score, according to PlayerProfiler.com. Washington also had a 39-inch vertical jump. The speed-power combination Washington can deliver is exquisite.

Washington doesn't offer much upside as a pass catcher, since Jeanty excels in that area and will still be used in a pass-catching role. Washington has had fumbling issues in the past, he has a bad habit of turning his back to contact, and he's not much of a pass blocker.

Time will tell whether this RB arrangement holds for the Raiders. It's possible Jeanty returns to a workhorse role if he shows improvement or if Washington fails in his expanded role. But rushing volume is worth chasing on waivers, and Washington appears poised to get substantial rushing volume in the weeks to come.

Washington is about to get a run of tough matchups, with the 49ers, Seahawks and Broncos up next on the schedule. But if you're weak at running back, Washington is worth a robust FAAB bid this week.

players.name: Eli Raridon
players.waiver_note:
Eli Raridon could be a short-term option at tight end if Hunter Henry is sidelined. Henry left the Patriots' Week 8 win over the Dolphins with a foot injury.

If Henry is out, New England could be missing a ton of pass-catching firepower in Week 9. AJ Brown missed Week 8 with ankle and knee problems, and WRs Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins are on IR (although Hollins is eligible to come off this week).

A third-round pick out of Notre Dame, Raridon has 13-173-2 on 20 targets.

players.name: Chris Rodriguez Jr.
players.waiver_note: Bhayshul Tuten has taken the lead-back role in Jacksonville and run with it, but Chris Rodriguez Jr. has handcuff value and perhaps a touch of stand-alone value in standard-scoring leagues. Rodriguez is a zero as a pass catcher, but he's a human hammer of a runner who's effective at the goal line. Rodriguez, who spent one season playing for Jaguars head coach Liam Coen at the University of Kentucky when Coen was the Wildcats' offensive coordinator, got his third touchdown run of the season in Week 8.

players.name: Kaelon Black
players.waiver_note:
Frankly, it's surprising that Kaelon Black is rostered in only 31% of Yahoo leagues. Christian McCaffrey strained his hamstring in Week 7 and briefly left the 49ers' Week 7 loss to the Falcons. Black played a season-high 47% snap share in that game and had 12-63-1 rushing.

The reporting has been optimistic about McCaffrey's injury, suggesting it's only minor and that McCaffrey should be good to go against the Raiders when San Francisco emerges from its Week 8 bye.

But 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan hasn't always been entirely forthright about McCaffrey's injuries. In the late summer of 2024, Shanahan expressed little public concern about a McCaffrey injury that was described as calf tightness. It turned out CMC had Achilles tendinitis in both feet. He went on injured reserve and didn't play his first game of the season until November.

The third running back selected in this year's draft and the only RB drafted in either the second or third rounds, Black has been impressive as a runner thus far, with 233 yards and a touchdown on 57 carries. He has an excellent 57.9% rushing success rate, per Fantasy Points Data, and is slightly above league average in rushing yards over expected par carry and yards after contact per carry.

Black is a physical runner, but unlike Kamikaze-style ball carriers such as Isiah Pacheco, Black actually has good run vision. The rookie isn't much of a pass-catcher, though — or at least he hasn't shown much aptitude in that area thus far. Black has three catches for four yards.

An excellent speculative add in case McCaffrey's injury snowballs into something significant, Black is worth a hearty FAAB bid if he's still available in your league.

players.name: Kendre Miller
players.waiver_note:
Bid no more than $1 on Kendre Miller, and only if you're desperate at running back.

The Saints haven't been able to run the ball. As a team, they have rushed for 55 or fewer yards in three of their last four games. The Saints' running game ranks 30th in defense-adjusted value over average (DVOA). When we last saw Miller before the Saints' Week 8 bye, he had eight carries for six yards against the Steelers.

Travis Etienne Jr. has been on IR with a hamstring injury and is eligible to come off IR this week. If we get word before waiver claims are due that Etienne will return this week, don't bother claiming Miller.

But if Etienne isn't ready to come back yet, Miller would be an option for the truly RB-needy this week. His matchup against the Browns is no better than neutral, but Miller has had 38 carries over his last three games.

players.name: Seth McGowan
players.waiver_note:
Saddled with a poor record and going nowhere fast, the Indianapolis Colts began selling off parts last week, trading OG Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks and DT DeForest Buckner to the 49ers. RB Jonathan Taylor is rumored to be available as well, and if he's dealt, rookie Seth McGowan would become the Colts' No. 1 running back.

A seventh-round pick out of Kentucky, McGowan has 37-163-0 rushing and 4-12-0 receiving on five targets. He won a training-camp battle with second-year man DJ Giddens to be Taylor's primary backup.

McGowan, who just turned 25, has good size at 6-0, 223, and isn't easy to bring down. He's a good athlete who clocked a 4.49 at the scouting combine and had a 42.5-inch vertical jump.

The question is how much fantasy value a lead-back role with the white-flag-waving Colts would yield. Touch volume at the RB position is important, of course, but McGowan's TD potential might be limited even in a lead role, and the overall ineptitude of the Colts' offense might cap his value.

McGowan is certainly an interesting speculative play, but don't completely blow out the FAAB budget to acquire a largely untested rookie in an oxygen-starved ecosystem.

players.name: Samaje Perine
players.waiver_note: Samaje Perine briefly flirted with stand-alone fantasy value, but he's really just a handcuff to Chase Brown. As potent as the Cincinnati offense is, Perine is one of the more essential RB handcuffs in fantasy.

players.name: Emmett Johnson
players.waiver_note: Impetuous fantasy managers might be tempted to splurge on Emmett Johnson after his banner receiving performance in Week 8. Johnson had 5-128-1 on five targets, scoring on a screen pass that went for 73 yards. But there's no reliable stand-alone value here. Johnson played 12 of the Chiefs' 68 offensive snaps on Sunday. He is, however, a key handcuff. Johnson is the top backup to Kenneth Walker III and would become immensely valuable if Walker were to miss time. Just don't overbid.

players.name: Kenyon Sadiq
players.waiver_note:
Check the status of Mason Taylor before bidding on Kenyon Sadiq. Taylor left the Jets' Week 8 loss to the Raiders with an apparent leg injury. If it's only minor and Taylor isn't expected to miss time, it's probably not worth adding Sadiq.

However, if Mason is going to miss multiple games, Sadiq could be a worthwhile add.

The rookie flashed earlier this season with a 7-105-1 game against the Lions. Sadiq, the 16th overall pick of this year's draft, is an athletic unicorn with 4.39 speed and a 43.5-inch vertical jump.

The Jets have a fine trio of wide receivers in Garrett Wilson, Omar Cooper Jr. and Adonai Mitchell. If Mason is around as well, there's simply too much target competition for Sadiq to provide anything close to consistent fantasy value. But if Taylor is out? Maybe.

The Jets have favorable TE matchups the next two weeks with games against the Chiefs and Bills. Entering Week 8, the Chiefs had given up the seventh-most half-point PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends, the Bills the 14th-most.

But again, check Taylor's injury status before placing a claim on Sadiq.

players.name: Gunnar Helm
players.waiver_note: Titans TE Gunnar Helm had his best game of the season in Week 8, with 5-76-0 receiving on nine targets. But Helm hadn't produced more than 28 receiving yards in any other game this season, and the Titans don't exactly have a high-octane passing attack. Plus, Tennessee will be on bye in Week 9.

players.name: Terrance Ferguson
players.waiver_note:
Terrance Ferguson has been on IR with a high-ankle sprain. He was eligible to come off IR in Week 8, but the Rams chose not to open his 21-day window to return. It's possible they'll designate him to return this week.

An athletic second-year tight end with 4.63 speed and a 39-inch vertical jump, Ferguson had 6-54-1 on nine targets against the Giants in Week 2 when the Rams were without Puka Nacua. Now, the Rams are without Davante Adams, who's expected to miss about two months with a hamstring injury.

The Rams badly need a credible No. 2 pass-catcher behind Nacua. Ferguson can be that guy. Anyone with a need at tight end should consider making a run at Ferguson this week.
